text: PREFACE This new edition contains new words and senses that have become established in the language since publication of the pre¬ vious edition.
text_raw:
PREFACE 
This new edition contains new words and senses that have 
become established in the language since publication of the pre¬ 
vious edition.

text: It remains an extremely concise reference to those words that form the very core of the English vocabulary.
text_raw:
It remains an extremely concise reference to those 
words that form the very core of the English vocabulary.

text: It is intended to serve as a quick reference, especially for questions of spelling, pronunciation, and hyphenation of the most common words in everyday use.
text_raw:
It is 
intended to serve as a quick reference, especially for questions of 
spelling, pronunciation, and hyphenation of the most common 
words in everyday use.

text: Though small, this work shares many details of presentation with more comprehensive dictionaries.
text_raw:
Though small, this work shares many details of presentation 
with more comprehensive dictionaries.

text: However, conciseness of presentation necessarily requires special treatment of entries, and this book has a number of special features uniquely its own.
text_raw:
However, conciseness of 
presentation necessarily requires special treatment of entries, and 
this book has a number of special features uniquely its own.

text: Users need to be familiar with the following major features of this dic¬ tionary.
text_raw:
Users 
need to be familiar with the following major features of this dic¬ 
tionary.

text: Main entries follow one another in alphabetical order.
text_raw: Main entries follow one another in alphabetical order.

text: Centered periods within the entries show points at which a hyphen may be put when the word is broken at the end of a line.
text_raw:
Centered periods within the entries show points at which a hyphen 
may be put when the word is broken at the end of a line.

text: Homographs (words spelled the same but having different meanings) are run in to a single main entry when they are closely related.
text_raw:
Homographs (words spelled the same but having different 
meanings) are run in to a single main entry when they are closely 
related.

text: Second and succeeding homographs are represented by a swung dash: ^ Homographs of distinctly different origin (as Verch and *perch) are given separate entries with preceding raised numerals.
text_raw:
Second and succeeding homographs are represented by a 
swung dash: ^ Homographs of distinctly different origin (as 
Verch and *perch) are given separate entries with preceding 
raised numerals.

text: Variant spellings that are quite common appear at the main entry following a comma (as the-ater, the-atre) and following other boldface entry words, such as inflected forms and run-on entries.
text_raw:
Variant spellings that are quite common appear at the main 
entry following a comma (as the-ater, the-atre) and following 
other boldface entry words, such as inflected forms and run-on 
entries.

text: Inflected forms of norms, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are shown when they are irregular—as when requiring the dropping of a final e or changing a final y to i before the suffix:
text_raw:
Inflected forms of norms, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are 
shown when they are irregular—as when requiring the dropping 
of a final e or changing a final y to i before the suffix:

text: (as prat-ed; prat'ing at prate) or when the form of the base word itself changes:
(as swam...; swum at swim)—or when there might be doubt about their spelling:
text_raw:
(as swam...; swum at swim)—or when there might be 
doubt about their spelling:

text: (as pi twos at two).
text_raw: (as pi twos at two).

text: They are given either in full (as worse...; worst at bad) or cut back to a con¬ venient point of division (as -mat-ed; -mat-ing at es-ti-mate).
text_raw:
They are given 
either in full (as worse...; worst at bad) or cut back to a con¬ 
venient point of division (as -mat-ed; -mat-ing at es-ti-mate).

text: Common variants of inflected forms are shown even if they are regular (as bused or bussed at bus).
text_raw:
Common variants of inflected forms are shown even if they are 
regular (as bused or bussed at bus).

text: When the inflected forms of a verb involve no irregularity except the doubling of a final
text_raw:
When the inflected forms 
of a verb involve no irregularity except the doubling of a final

text: consonant, the double consonant is shown instead of full or cut¬ back inflected forms (as vb -gg- at hug).
text_raw:
consonant, the double consonant is shown instead of full or cut¬ 
back inflected forms (as vb -gg- at hug).

text: A variant or inflected form whose alphabetical place is distant from the main entry is entered at its own place with a cross-reference in small capital let¬ ters to the main entry (as laid past of lay).
text_raw:
A variant or inflected 
form whose alphabetical place is distant from the main entry is 
entered at its own place with a cross-reference in small capital let¬ 
ters to the main entry (as laid past of lay).

text: Several other kinds of entries are also found in this dictionary.
text_raw: Several other kinds of entries are also found in this dictionary.

text: A run-in entry is a term related to a main entry that appears with¬ in a definition (as cacao beans at ca'cao).
text_raw:
A run-in entry is a term related to a main entry that appears with¬ 
in a definition (as cacao beans at ca'cao).

text: It is essentially defined in the context of the definition and is set off by parenthe¬ ses.
text_raw:
It is essentially 
defined in the context of the definition and is set off by parenthe¬ 
ses.

text: Derivative words, made up usually of the main entry and a common word element, such as a suffix, are shown as undefined run-on entries following all definitions of a main entry.
text_raw:
Derivative words, made up usually of the main entry and a 
common word element, such as a suffix, are shown as undefined 
run-on entries following all definitions of a main entry.

text: These are set off by a dash (as — man-u-al-ly at man-U'al or — hilhtop at hill).
text_raw:
These are 
set off by a dash (as — man-u-al-ly at man-U'al or — hilhtop at 
hill).

text: The meaning of an undefined run-on entry can be inferred from the meaning of the main entry where it appears and that of the added word element, shown elsewhere in the book.
text_raw:
The meaning of an undefined run-on entry can be inferred 
from the meaning of the main entry where it appears and that of 
the added word element, shown elsewhere in the book.

text: A run-on phrase is a group of two or more words having the main entry as a major element and having a special meaning of its own (as knock out at knock or set forth at set).
text_raw:
A run-on 
phrase is a group of two or more words having the main entry as 
a major element and having a special meaning of its own (as 
knock out at knock or set forth at set).

text: Run-on phrases are always defined.
text_raw:
Run-on phrases are 
always defined.

text: Pronunciation respellings are placed within reversed slanted lines (as \ijen3*ral9te\ at ge-ner-al-i*ty).

respellings are placed within reversed slanted lines (as

text: Where the pronunciation is not indicated at a particular entry, or is indicated in a cutback form, the full pronunciation is to be inferred from an earlier indicated pronunciation.

text: The grammatical function of entry words is indicated by an italic functional label (as vb, n, or prefix).

text: Guide words are used at the top of pages to indicate the range of entries on those pages.
text_raw:
Guide words are used at the top of pages to indicate the range

text: In choosing guide words for a page, we select the alphabetically first and last spelled-out boldface words or phrases on that page.
text_raw:
In choosing guide words for a page, we 
select the alphabetically first and last spelled-out boldface words 
or phrases on that page.

text: This means that any boldface entry— main entry, variant spelling, inflected form, run-in or run-on entry—can be used as a guide word.
text_raw:
This means that any boldface entry— 
main entry, variant spelling, inflected form, run-in or run-on 
entry—can be used as a guide word.

text: Please keep this in mind if the word used as a guide word does not happen to be the first or last main entry on fie page.

text: The guide words themselves are in alphabetical order throughout the book, so occasionally it has been necessary to modify this rule.

text: When the alphabetically last entry on one page would come later than the alphabetically first entry on the following page, a different word is chosen as guide word.
